New XERJ Query-1, answers that show their work →

The search engine built for AI agents.

One open-source binary that indexes your files, code and databases, and answers questions with the evidence attached. Runs offline on a CPU.

Give this to your AI agent
Set up XERJ for me, following https://xerj.org/llms.txt.
1. Install XERJ with the XERJ Query-1 model and start it.
2. Index the folder I point you to (ask before reading anything outside it) and run one search.
3. Write three facts from that data into a facts namespace and ask XERJ Query-1 one question about them. Show me the answer, the program and the evidence.
4. Set up reference coding: index one open-source repo close to this project and look up one definition in it.
5. If this client takes MCP servers, register XERJ (llms.txt has the line for each client) and save one memory note through it.
If you have no shell, use the HTTP or MCP steps in llms.txt instead.

Check it worked: curl -s localhost:9200/_facts | grep -o '"state":"loaded"' prints "state":"loaded" (empty for a few seconds while the model loads).

No shell: HTTP and MCP steps in llms.txt. Install it yourself: curl -fsSL https://xerj.org/get | sh -s -- --with-model on Linux and macOS; Windows and other targets: install.

How we measured

Why now

Agents now do a growing share of the searching. Every answer they get from a language model costs seconds and money, and comes back as text nobody checked. XERJ moves that work into the index: search in milliseconds, and answers computed as small programs over your own facts, each with the evidence it used.

For developers whose coding agents need real code, and for teams whose data cannot leave their network.

Programs, not prose.

XERJ Query-1 writes a short program and the engine runs it. No fact, no answer: it says UNKNOWN.

One binary, no stack.

Search, vectors, facts, memory and an Elasticsearch-compatible API in one Rust binary.

Your data stays put.

Runs offline on a CPU, on a laptop or a server inside your network.

A program on a CPU instead of a model call per question.

Use cases

One binary. Seven jobs.

01 · Answers

Answers you can check, or an honest UNKNOWN.

XERJ Query-1 turns a question into a short program and the engine runs it over facts you or your agent wrote. No backing facts: UNKNOWN. Facts that disagree: CONFLICT.

How XERJ Query-1 works

02 · Reference coding

Your coding agent stops guessing APIs.

Index the open-source repos closest to what you build, and on code it hasn't memorised your coding agent reads the real definition instead of inventing one and looping. Ready-made corpora are on the Corpus Hub.

2.7x fewer output tokens

than Claude Code grepping the same source, both 16 of 16 solved; 8 tasks in 4 languages on libraries written for the test. On code the model already knows, retrieval saved nothing.

The case study

03 · Search

Every file in a folder or bucket, searchable and cited.

xerj autoindex identifies each file by its content and indexes PDF, Office, HTML, CSV, JSON, email exports, SQLite, SQL dumps and code, from a folder or from S3, R2 or MinIO. Full-text and hybrid search.

4.6 s

to make 13 public NIST and CMS PDFs (22.9 MB, 3,032 records) searchable with the rc.101 release on a 32-core x86_64 laptop; then 0.9 ms at p50 over 200 different two-word searches. Run 2026-11-07.

Zero-config autoindex

04 · Live data Ships in rc.102

Search what your database says right now.

xerj connect postgres://... takes a consistent snapshot, then follows every insert, update and delete through Postgres logical replication, and picks up again after a restart.

19.7 ms

median from Postgres commit to readable in XERJ, 60 updates on a 200,000-row synthetic table, Postgres 16 (p95 21.7 ms; run 2026-11-05).

The worked example

05 · Memory

Agents that remember, and show why.

Agents store, recall and forget notes, and link them into a graph where every edge keeps its evidence. Recall works by keyword and word overlap by default; turn on a neural encoder to recall by meaning.

24 MCP tools

on one node, next to search and facts (23 when XERJ Query-1 is off). Setup per client in llms.txt.

Agent memory recipe

06 · Enterprise on-prem Cohere hooks ship in rc.102

Search and answers inside your own network.

One XERJ node indexes your documents and databases on a CPU server you own, and passes the best hits to Cohere Rerank, Embed and Command, at a private endpoint, only when you turn them on. XERJ is not affiliated with Cohere.

787 MB of RAM

for the search node holding a live 200,000-row table, 3,033 document records and their vectors; the node running XERJ Query-1 used 1.05 GB (run 2026-11-05). Cohere calls were tested against a mock of Cohere's API.

Cohere on XERJ

07 · Bridge

Keep your Elasticsearch clients. Change the engine.

XERJ answers the Elasticsearch 8.x REST API for indexing, search, aggregations and kNN, so existing clients and scripts can keep working while you move to the native API. It is its own engine, written from scratch in Rust.

0 failed

in our Elasticsearch 8.x conformance suite on main: 1,448 of 1,458 cases passed, 10 skipped (CI, 2026-11-07). No client version matrix yet, and the Python client's bulk helper sends PUT /_bulk, which rc.101 refuses; POST works (fix: #3036).
